A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same scale-equivariance research. Their text, equations, tables, figures, and complete appendices are readable, and retained material can be matched across relocation and renumbering.

before.justification: v1 reports original spectral analyses, generation and reconstruction experiments on ImageNet and Kinetics-700, and regularization ablations in the main text and appendices.

after.justification: v3 retains these original results and adds training-from-scratch experiments, noise-schedule and compute controls, further spectral analyses, and qualitative findings from unsuccessful approaches.

M1.justification: The proposed SE objective, bilinear downsampling, default regularization weight, and treatment of KL regularization remain unchanged. The expanded self-conditioning description documents an existing component; the rejected alternatives in Appendix E do not replace or modify the adopted method.

E1.justification: Both versions cover image and video generation, reconstruction, and spectral analysis using ImageNet-1K, Kinetics-700, and internal autoencoder-training data. ImageNet 512-resolution experiments already appear in v1. The new scratch-training and spectral studies extend protocols and model configurations within this coverage.

E2.justification: The main benchmark comparator sets remain unchanged. New Appendix E reports qualitative comparisons of decoder R1/Lipschitz regularization against SE and joint mini-LDM training against vanilla training. AF-LDM is newly cited as related work, not evaluated as a baseline.

E3.justification: v3 adds same-data scratch-training protocols, noise-distribution and inference-time shifting sweeps evaluated with 128 unguided steps, and a 20K-versus-10K autoencoder-training control. Table 7 also changes the reported backbone from DiT-B/1 to DiT-B/2 while retaining its scores; this establishes a reported setting correction, not that experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: New analyses test schedule and compute explanations for the gains, effectiveness when training from scratch, and spectral behavior under noise and across WanAE/LTX-AE configurations. Figure 4 expands SE-strength spectral analysis, and Appendix E documents unsuccessful alternatives. Conversely, Figure 9 removes the SSIM-versus-regularization-strength panel.

E5.justification: Both versions describe averaging spectral profiles over 256 samples and already display shaded spectral bands. v3 adds no explicit seed counts, repeated-run reporting, confidence intervals, significance tests, or explanation of the bands' statistical meaning.

E6.justification: Existing Tables 1–4 and 6–9 retain their numerical entries, but v3 adds substantial results in Table 10, Figure 10, and the compute analysis, and revises spectral curves. In the new scratch-training comparison, FluxAE generation FID5K is 25.43 without SE versus 22.32 with SE; CogVideoX-AE generation FVD5K is 336.33 versus 237.28. Reconstruction PSNR falls from 29.39 to 28.73 and 37.08 to 36.61, respectively. These are newly reported comparisons, not improvements over v1 under identical settings.

T1.justification: Appendix E adds an ELBO decomposition and a cited Wasserstein-error bound to motivate alternative regularizers. Appendix B defines the inference-time shifting transformation. The existing DCT, SE, frequency-cutoff, and soft-penalty mathematics remain equivalent; no new original proof is supplied.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same central spectral-diffusability hypothesis and SE contribution, including the headline 19% FID and at least 44% FVD reductions. The additional experiments support these retained claims rather than redefining them.

C2.justification: v3 adds a channel-capacity explanation for high-frequency content, discusses schedule and compute explanations, and identifies practical or applicability limits of mini-LDM, Lipschitz, and temporal SE approaches. The original limitations list merely moves from Appendix D to A. The new time-shifting discussion and Figure 10 caption contain contradictory wording that says the gains are 'not due to improved diffusability,' leaving their stated interpretation unclear.

D1.justification: v3 adds a source-code link and specifies existing self-conditioning details, including the 90% auxiliary-pass probability, projected final-block activations, and no-gradient execution. It completes the cached-video-clip explanation and documents time shifting, new experiment budgets, and fvcore compute measurement. The established hyperparameter table and hardware information remain unchanged.

R1.justification: The concurrent-work discussion adds AF-LDM and expands its description of EQ-VAE to scale/shift equivariance. Additional references support self-conditioning, time shifting, error propagation, WanAE, and R1 regularization. The overall positioning around spectral diffusability remains intact.

P1.justification: Most existing prose and the main section sequence are retained. Changes include localized explanatory rewrites, correction of Table 7's regularizer description, moving limitations to the beginning of the appendices, and adding subsections for experiments and visualizations.

P2.justification: Several central displays are substantially revised: Figures 2–3 switch from logarithmic to linear amplitude axes, Figure 4 expands its curves, Figures 8–9 are reformatted, and Figure 9 loses its SSIM panel. v3 adds the time-shifting plot, noise and video-autoencoder spectral figures, and Table 10. Existing sample galleries are retained and renumbered.

improvement.justification: v3 strengthens the existing evidence with schedule and compute controls and same-data scratch-training validation, while improving implementation documentation and code-access information. These make the retained claims better tested and easier to reproduce. The gains are tempered by the contradictory time-shifting interpretation and limited discussion of Table 10's reconstruction losses, yielding an incremental overall improvement.
